messages:
leah: quick dump from a bring‑up run for cerulean9b (fp16 / int6 / int8). ran the standard GTN longform slice + short chat subset. notes below.

james: awesome — any big regressions we should flag to product?

leah: short answer: slight longform drift on int8 vs fp16, but int8 wins on token econ for short responses. details: 

leah: ```
Benchmark slice: 2k prompts (mix longform 32% / short 68%)
- fp16 (baseline): p95 latency 210ms, tokens/s 420, unit cost $0.054 / 1k toks, quality delta 0.0%
- int6: p95 230ms, tokens/s 380, unit cost $0.038 / 1k toks, quality delta -0.8% (mainly longform)
- int8: p95 250ms, tokens/s 330, unit cost $0.025 / 1k toks, quality delta -2.1% (longform NLG drift)

Signal: longform QA and chain-of-thought prompts drop more for int8 (avg knock ~2.7% on ROUGE-like metric). Short chat/intent classification unchanged within noise.
```

tara: can you paste sample failure? want to see hallucination / truncation examples.

leah: pasted one below (truncated to keep inline):
leah: "User: summarize the paper and list open questions
FP16: gives concise summary + correct 6 open questions
INT8: summary ok but invents 1 extra method in open questions (hallucination)"

matt: hmm. interesting — latency degradation from fp16->int8 is a bit surprising (I expected int8 to be faster). were kernels optimal?

leah: tuned kernels for int8 but we're seeing kv-cache overhead and extra dequant ops for long contexts. for short chat int8 is faster overall because batching improves throughput.

rachel: from product/GTN POV: what's the recommendation for routing in mixed traffic?

leah: preliminary recs: 
- default route: int6 for mixed/longform workloads (best cost/quality balance)
- short-chat (<200 tokens): int8 with tighter quality monitoring; set fallback to int6 on regression triggers.
- safety/critical flows: pin to fp16.

james: propose feature flags: 
- routing.rule=prefer_int6
- canary.percent=5
- fallback_policy=auto_promote_fp16_on_quality_drop

leah: added a quick unit econ calc: assume 1M tokens/day (mixed traffic 30% longform)
leah: fp16 cost/day ~$54
leah: int6 cost/day ~$38 (−30%)
leah: int8 cost/day ~$25 (−54%) but expected QA hit for longform -> product risk.

eval-bot: automated evals: longform-suite drift metric exceeded threshold for int8 (score −2.1%) at 6550001290

matt: ok we should schedule a 30m sync with GTN to show the sample regressions + propose the routing flags.

rachel: can you prepare a 1‑slide scorecard: 3 cols (fp16 / int6 / int8) with p95, unit_cost, longform_delta, recommended_routes? I'll take to GTN.

leah: will do. adding a short checklist for rollout: 
- add routing flags in staging, start 5% int8 for short chat only
- wire eval hooks (longform suite) to alerting -> auto rollback for >1.5% drop
- create product-facing one-pager with sample failure + econ table

james: thumbs up. when you have the slide ping @rachel and I'll help with the economics numbers. :thumbsup:

leah: ping when slide is ready. thanks all.
